skill.displayName: TikTok-店铺商品列表 | 青虎AI

llm.summary: The skill’s TikTok shop lookup purpose is coherent, but it directs broad local tool installation and persistent credential setup without clear user-controlled setup boundaries.

dimensions.detail: Downloading Node, unpacking it under the user home directory, changing PATH, optionally using mirrors, and running npm global installs expand local execution surface for a read-only data retrieval skill, even though the behavior is disclosed and partly verified by SHA256 for Node.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions tell the agent to install qhkit globally, use unpinned npx fallback, install Node from remote downloads if absent, and upgrade to latest versions; this is broader than the narrow lookup task and lacks clear confirmation before modifying the host environment.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill has broad trigger wording and says it must trigger for similar shop-product or competitor requests; it does require asking for missing required inputs and consent before paid calls, but setup actions are not similarly gated.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs qhkit config set --token and environment variable setup for API credentials, creating authentication state that can persist beyond the immediate lookup task.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose, querying TikTok shop product lists by seller_id through qhkit, matches the described commands and paid data flow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use this skill only if you intend to use the Qinghu qhkit paid data service, and do the Node/qhkit installation and token setup yourself or only after explicit approval. Prefer pinned package versions and avoid storing API tokens in persistent local config unless you are comfortable with later qhkit calls using that credential.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad trigger language is artifact-backed; the skill also narrows actual use to tiktok_seller_product_list and requires seller_id, so this is a scoping concern rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The environment bootstrap concern is supported by the artifact: it instructs installing qhkit, Node, PATH setup, and upgrades when dependencies are absent.
[RP1] unexpected: The artifact uses unpinned @iqinghu/qhkit in npm/npx examples and @latest for upgrades, creating reproducibility and supply-chain risk, but not showing deception or exfiltration.
[RA2] unexpected: The home-directory Node install and PATH export are present; this is disclosed setup persistence, not a hidden backdoor, but it is high-impact for a narrow lookup skill.
[SDI-2] expected: Credential configuration is necessary for the paid qhkit service, but writing a token into local config or environment is sensitive and should be explicitly user-directed.
